title: Our culture is way too eager to embrace deception
gist: Yglesias, using the Elizabeth Holmes documentary 'You Can See Everything', argues that lying is universal but US culture, including Silicon Valley, has become too tolerant of dishonesty and misleading behavior. Only the opening of the paywalled piece is available.

insights.claim: Whatever separates Elizabeth Holmes from many celebrated tech CEOs cannot simply be that she said untrue things about her product and company, because lots of successful entrepreneurs lie.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Fraud-enforcement lines in startup culture are blurry; selective prosecution and reputational risk for founders who overpromise.

insights.claim: Although nearly everyone agrees lying is bad, everybody lies, so claiming to never lie is itself the most obviously dishonest statement a person can make.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Treat absolute honesty claims by executives as a red flag in diligence.
insights.quote: the most obviously dishonest thing a person could do, genuinely, is claim to never lie

insights.claim: Despite the universality of white lies, American culture has become too tolerant of dishonesty and especially of willfully misleading behavior, and needs to rebuild an ethic of probity and integrity.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Suggests rising governance and integrity discount may be underpriced for promotional founder-led companies.
